correctness.rationale: For every finite m>=2 and iid-in-time centered independent edge coefficients bounded |xi|<=rho<1, the simplex is invariant and all coordinates X_i are bounded martingales and hence converge a.s. Skew symmetry conserves total mass. Expanding H=sum_i X_i^2 gives exact conditional drift 2 sum_{ij in E} E[xi_ij^2] X_i^2 X_j^2, since cross-edge covariances vanish. Its expected sum is bounded by H<=1 and implies each edge endpoint product tends to zero a.s. Thus the limiting support is an independent set; every such face is pointwise fixed and all stationary measures on the compact simplex must be supported on these faces by zero integrated drift. Complete G iff only vertices survive for every starting x; winning law follows from E X_infty=x. For strictly positive initial x, on winner event I=i, the loser log-increments differ Cesaro-negligibly from iid log(1+xi_ji), giving negative exponent by strong law and Jensen. Complete multipartite part masses likewise martingales. Independent exact-rational two-edge example conditional drift 277/36450 matches formula; finite checks do not substitute for martingale theorem.

The sharp sparse graph invariant-law and complete-graph iff, with winner probabilities and almost-sure extinction rates, remain distinct under inspected statements.
